content:
AnnalsChallenge is a dataset of formal theorem statements. The theorems are all from 2020s papers from the Annals of Mathematics.

This is the first significant public output from the Renaissance Philanthropy-funded grant A dataset of modern formalised theorem statements, although the team also made many mathlib PRs in order to make this dataset possible.

It is a natural challenge for AI (or for humans) to give end-to-end formalisations of the sorries in this dataset. The difficulty of the sorries ranges from "it's been formalized in Lean already" to "it would need 10000 pages of background material before one could even start", so it's quite a range.

Another challenge, which the team will be working on in the next academic year, is to get more 2020s Annals statements formalized. This is becoming a difficult task because mathlib is still missing many fundamental definitions which show up in Annals papers.

The statements of the theorems will, in the near future, be included in lean-eval.

The team who put this dataset together is: @Thomas Browning , @Katy Hristova , @David Ledvinka and @Justus Springer , together with summer interns @Hang Lu Su and @Jack McKoen . They were overseen by @Kevin Buzzard .

Questions about the project should be asked in the discussion thread
